records.name: Antonija
records.facts_used: Antonija: The documented family leads to Latin Antonius, an ancient Roman family name. Its further meaning is not securely established. The popular comparison with Greek anthos, flower, is therefore not a proved original translation of this name family. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Antonija: 1832, Rūjiena. Its calendar year is 1767. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact feminine Antonius family secure; ultimate meaning explicitly unknown. No flower/priceless derivation adopted. Own1832 and calendar 1767 distinguished.

records.name: Anta
records.facts_used: Anta: Siliņš distinguishes two Anta entries: masculine Anta/Ante is linked to Antons, feminine Anta to Antonija. Both lead to Latin Antonius, whose further meaning is not securely known. The gendered examples should remain separate rather than making one the origin of every bearer. The dictionary records masculine Anta/Ante at Mārciena in 1562 and feminine Anta at Lubāna in 1930. The feminine entry gives the calendar year 1932. This distinction keeps the earlier masculine date from being transferred to the feminine name.

records.uncertainties: Siliņš pp61/62 two genders explicitly retained;1932 belongs feminine entry. Root unknown explicitly, no speculative literal translation.

records.name: Ambraziejus
records.facts_used: Ambraziejus: The Lithuanian form continues Greek Ambrosios, immortal, through the Latin Ambrosius tradition. The family spread in Europe among Christian names. The ancient designation belongs to linguistic and cultural history rather than literally describing a person’s lifespan. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Ambraziejus (Ambras, Ambrazas, Brazys) on 7 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original SalysPDF318printed303December7; exact form, not every variant’s first attestation.

records.name: Sabiine
records.facts_used: Sabiine: The family is based on Latin Sabina, the feminine of Sabinus. It referred to the Sabines, a people of ancient Italy. This is an ethnic designation in the name’s history, not a statement about a modern bearer’s nationality or personal qualities. The first page of Leole’s December 2005 issue uses the exact spelling Sabiine. The local name column shows that this form was discussed in Estonian print. This dated evidence is neither a first birth record nor the year the name was invented.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact Estonian dictionary and December 2005p1 both connect Sabiine with LatinSabina. No date transferred from Latvian Sabīne.
